chapter_summary: Debolina moves through rooms whose former life survives only in fragments. The haveli shifts her attention from possession to what remains after departure.

history.status: grounded in the declared setting only
flagged_uncertainties: No specific haveli, patron family, or construction date is named in the source; the poem must not date the house or assign it an owner.

spatality.place: an abandoned haveli in Mandawa, entered from the lane side
spatality.route: outer courtyard to inner rooms, each smaller and darker
spatality.texture: hollow corridors, plaster fallen from the ceiling, cool air with no source

poetic_parameters.movement: Language Poetry — the room as a field of fragments, meaning delayed and spatial.
writing_skills: walking syntax, where each room is a clause
a close that hands the emptiness back to the reader
poetic_parameters.image_seed: a hanging rope from which a swing has been cut down, the fray still visible
poetic_parameters.volta: from reading emptiness as absence to reading it as a kind of continued occupation
poetic_parameters.sonic_texture: hollow o and r in room, door, floor, and the flatness of dust
poetic_parameters.line_gesture: long walking lines that slow at each doorway, ending on one very short line
poetic_parameters.variety_note: Part three opens outward into other people's lives; this is the first poem where Debolina is a visitor rather than the sole inhabitant of the night.
poetic_parameters.metaphor_family: departure as architecture — rooms shaped around who has left
poetic_parameters.address: the house itself, in the second person
poetic_parameters.closing_move: an image of the swing's cut rope, offered as the poem's last fact
